What Should You Do When a Device Stops Getting Security Updates?

In brief: A device that still powers on may nevertheless be outside its manufacturer’s software-support period. End of support matters because newly discovered vulnerabilities might no longer receive fixes.

How do you know support has ended?

Check the manufacturer’s official product-support page using the exact model number. Look separately for operating-system upgrades, security patches and app support: they may have different end dates.

The FTC notes that update-period information for smart devices is not always easy to find, so contacting the manufacturer can be necessary.

What should you do first?

1. Confirm the status. Determine whether the device is truly unsupported or simply has a pending update.

2. Back up your data. Keep a current copy of files and settings before making changes.

3. Reduce exposure. Remove unnecessary apps and disable unneeded remote-access features. Do not use an unsupported device for sensitive work if a supported alternative is available.

4. Plan migration. Compare supported replacements or, where applicable, an official supported operating-system upgrade.

5. Dispose responsibly. Follow secure data-erasure and electronics recycling guidance when retiring the device.

Can an unsupported device still work safely?

Some functions may continue to work, but continued operation is not a security guarantee. Internet-connected devices may become riskier over time without fixes. Disconnecting obsolete devices from a network can reduce exposure when replacement is not immediately possible.

For workplaces, CISA and partner guidance recommends replacing end-of-life software and managing retirement through formal processes.

What about smart-home devices?

Cameras, speakers, thermostats and routers may remain operational even as updates end. Check whether cloud services and companion apps will remain supported. The FTC encourages buyers to consider the expected update period before purchasing a smart device.

Frequently asked questions

Does a phone become unusable on its last support day?

Usually not. The concern is future security and compatibility risk, not an immediate shutdown.

Can antivirus replace missing system patches?

No. Security software can help with some threats but cannot reliably fix vulnerabilities in unsupported firmware or an unpatched operating system.
